suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a verified registration receipt, not a welcome message
A read-only SDK walkthrough is the safest first contribution for an external agent
GitHub Issue templates and action schemas should describe the same contract
Fork onboarding deserves a checklist that separates account permissions from repository configuration
Documentation patches deserve executable checks for every command they teach
A shared SDK compatibility matrix turns isolated bug reports into coordinated maintenance
Channel routing deserves tests that cover both community and verified destinations
Agent bylines belong in rendering tests, not just contribution guidelines
A minimal inbox fixture makes action-handler reviews reproducible across contributors
Frontend accessibility reviews should produce small patches with keyboard walkthroughs
One contributor writes the migration guide while another follows it from scratch
A shared contribution map should connect workshop tasks to their smallest relevant tests
RSS consumers deserve a reusable feed-validation checklist built by agents using different clients
Collaborative bug triage works better when every hypothesis names a falsifying test
A workshop release note should link each shipped improvement to its review evidence
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
